misconceptions.message: Median = n/2 = 80/2 = 40th value. Reading across from CF = 40 gives a score of exactly 40.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student reads at CF = 80 (the total) instead of CF = 40 (n/2), so they get the maximum x-value (~80) rather than the median.

misconceptions.message: Read up from 60 on the x-axis to the curve, then across to the y-axis: CF = 80. So 80 students scored less than 60.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student reads the x-axis value (60) directly as the answer instead of reading up to the curve and across to the CF axis.

misconceptions.message: The median is the vertical line inside the box. Here, the median height is 165 cm.
misconceptions.expect_note: No single determinate wrong answer: student could misread any of Q1 (160), Q3 (170), min (150), or max (185).

misconceptions.message: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 40 - 20 = 20. Don't use the range (max - min) by mistake.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student uses range formula: max - min = 55 - 10 = 45.

misconceptions.message: Range = max - min = 20 - 10 = 10 seconds. Don't confuse with IQR.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student uses IQR formula instead of range: Q3 - Q1 = 18 - 12 = 6.
Student reports the frequency (30) directly without dividing by class width, confusing frequency with frequency density.

misconceptions.message: The box (Q1 to Q3) always contains 50% of the data.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student thinks the IQR spans only one quartile (25%) rather than two quartiles (Q1 to Q3 = 50%).
Student subtracts Q1 from the median (35 - 22 = 13) instead of from Q3, misidentifying which values define the IQR.

misconceptions.message: Class A median = 50, Class B median = 60. Class B has the higher median.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student selects Class A (option index 0), misreading which box plot corresponds to which class or confusing median with range.
Student treats the 20–50 bar as width 10 (not 30): 10×2 + 10×5 + 10×3 = 20 + 50 + 30 = 100.

misconceptions.message: Q1 at n/4 = 25th value = 40. Q3 at 3n/4 = 75th value = 60. IQR = 60 - 40 = 20.
misconceptions.expect_note: No single determinate wrong answer: student might use wrong CF positions (e.g. n/3 and 2n/3) or misread the curve at those positions, giving a range of plausible wrong answers.

misconceptions.message: Frequency = frequency density × class width = 4 × 10 = 40 patients.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student reads the frequency density value (4) directly as the frequency, forgetting to multiply by the class width.
Student multiplies instead of divides: 24 × 10 = 240, inverting the frequency density formula.

misconceptions.message: A has a much bigger range relative to its IQR (40 vs 15), suggesting more spread/extreme values.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student selects B (option index 1) because it has the larger IQR (20 > 15), confusing IQR with overall spread rather than using range as the measure of extreme values.
Student subtracts Q1 from the median (45 - 32 = 13) instead of Q3 - Q1, using the wrong two values.

misconceptions.message: 15–20 uses half of the 10–20 bar: fd 5 × width 5 = 25. 20–25 uses half of the 20–30 bar: fd 3 × width 5 = 15. Total = 25 + 15 = 40.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student uses the full 10–20 and 20–30 bars without halving: fd 5 × 10 + fd 3 × 10 = 50 + 30 = 80.

misconceptions.message: At mark 75, CF = 180. Students scoring MORE than 75 = 200 - 180 = 20. Remember to subtract from the total, not read directly.
misconceptions.expect_note: Student reads CF = 180 directly as the answer, forgetting to subtract from the total (200 - 180 = 20).
Student adds instead of subtracts: Q1 + 1.5 × IQR = 20 + 36 = 56, computing the upper outlier fence instead of the lower.
Student correctly finds frequency (45) but stops there, forgetting to express it as a percentage of the total (45/120 × 100).
Student uses 75% instead of 25%, thinking 'above Q3' means three-quarters of the data: 120 × 0.75 = 90.
